evidence.title: International Thomas Merton Society
evidence.text: The International Thomas Merton Society, founded in 1987, is a learned society which studies the works of American Catholic writer and mystic Thomas Merton.

evidence.title: International Thomas Merton Society
evidence.text: It sponsors conferences and co-publishes a journal, "The Merton Seasonal".

evidence.title: International Thomas Merton Society
evidence.text: The society and the Thomas Merton Center are located at Bellarmine University in Louisville, Kentucky, U.S.A.

evidence.title: Thomas Merton Award
evidence.text: The Thomas Merton Award has been awarded since 1972 by the Thomas Merton Center for Peace and Social Justice in Pittsburgh, United States.

evidence.title: Thomas Merton Award
evidence.text: It is named after Thomas Merton and is given annually to "national and international individuals struggling for justice."

evidence.title: Somerset Maugham Award
evidence.text: The Somerset Maugham Award is a British literary prize given each May by the Society of Authors.

evidence.title: Somerset Maugham Award

evidence.title: Somerset Maugham Award

evidence.title: Somerset Maugham Award

evidence.title: Robert Calder (writer)
evidence.text: Robert Lorin Calder, a Canadian writer and professor, won the Governor General's Award for English-language non-fiction in 1989 for his "Willie: The Life of W. Somerset Maugham", a biography based on extensive archival work and interviews with surviving associates of Maugham, in particular Alan Searle.

evidence.title: Robert Calder (writer)
evidence.text: Unlike Ted Morgan, who had obtained permission from Maugham's executors to publish from Maugham's letters in his biography (1980), Calder was refused permission to do so by the Royal Literary Fund and had to rely on paraphrase in referencing Maugham's unpublished correspondence.

evidence.title: St. Joseph's Intermediate and Commercial School
evidence.text: St. Joseph's Intermediate and Commercial School (St. Joseph's Commercial School, SJICS, or St. Joe's Sherbourne) is a former Catholic High school located in the Cabbagetown neighbourhood of Toronto, Ontario, Canada part of the Metropolitan Separate School Board (now the Toronto Catholic District School Board).

evidence.title: Thomas Merton
evidence.text: Thomas Merton, O.C.S.O. (January 31, 1915 – December 10, 1968) was an American Catholic writer, theologian and mystic.

evidence.title: Thomas Merton
evidence.text: A Trappist monk of the Abbey of Gethsemani, Kentucky, he was a poet, social activist, and student of comparative religion.

evidence.title: Thomas Merton
evidence.text: In 1949, he was ordained to the priesthood and given the name Father Louis.

evidence.title: W. Somerset Maugham
evidence.text: William Somerset Maugham CH ( ; 25 January 1874 – 16 December 1965), better known as W. Somerset Maugham, was a British playwright, novelist and short story writer.

evidence.title: W. Somerset Maugham
evidence.text: He was among the most popular writers of his era and reputedly the highest-paid author during the 1930s.

evidence.title: Trio (film)
evidence.text: Trio (also known as W. Somerset Maugham's Trio) is a 1950 British anthology film based on three short stories by W. Somerset Maugham: "The Verger", "Mr. Know-All" and "Sanatorium".

evidence.title: Trio (film)
evidence.text: Ken Annakin directed "The Verger" and "Mr. Know-All", while Harold French was responsible for "Sanatorium".
